title: Reconstruct the GAN
summary: Recover the adversarial game between generator and discriminator, then implement stable binary cross-entropy objectives.

parts.title: A learned training signal
parts.prompt: How does a discriminator replace a fixed reconstruction loss for the generator?
parts.answer: The discriminator learns features that separate real from generated samples. Its gradient therefore supplies an adaptive signal about discrepancies that matter for distinguishing the two distributions.
hints: The loss network changes during training.
No paired target image is required.

parts.title: The minimax equilibrium
parts.prompt: What should the discriminator output when the generated distribution exactly matches the data distribution?
parts.answer: Real and generated samples are then indistinguishable, so the optimal discriminator outputs 0.5 everywhere. Neither source can be identified better than chance.
hints: Apply Bayes classification with equal source priors.
The generator wins by matching distributions.

parts.title: Why non-saturating loss?
parts.prompt: Why is minimizing -log D(G(z)) preferred over minimizing log(1-D(G(z))) early in training?
parts.answer: When the discriminator confidently rejects fakes, the original minimax generator objective can have weak gradients. The non-saturating objective strongly rewards increasing D(G(z)) and supplies a healthier early signal.
hints: Compare derivatives when D(G(z)) is near zero.
Both objectives target the same equilibrium.

parts.title: Implement discriminator loss
parts.prompt: Compute mean BCE for real probabilities against one and fake probabilities against zero.
